subject: Post-demo: budgeting, SLO tiers & routing options
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alex Navarro <alex@insightai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: budgeting, SLO tiers & routing options

Alex — thanks for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on budget / latency trade-offs.

Key notes from the call:
- Primary workload: conversational agent (support triage) with ~120M tokens/month initially, growing to ~600M over 12 months.
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 400ms for short queries (~64 tokens), but willing to accept 800–1200ms for rarer long-context calls during off-peak.
- Compliance: InsightAI needs SOC2 evidence and audit logs retained 12 months.
- Procurement: procurement@insightai.com will lead contract and needs a pricing band for $/1M tokens and committed vs on-demand options.

Cost/Unit economics we discussed (ballpark from the demo):
- Streaming / low-latency tier (SLO 95p < 400ms): estimated $1,200–$1,600 per 1M tokens depending on model variant and routing policy.
- Balanced tier (SLO 95p 400–800ms, batching allowed): estimated $450–$700 per 1M tokens.
- Throughput/batch-optimized tier (SLO relaxed > 800ms, heavy batching): estimated $150–$300 per 1M tokens.

Routing/implementation options I recommend for you to hit both latency and cost targets:
1) Hybrid routing: route 70–80% of traffic through balanced tier (auto-batched), pin high-SLA traffic (interactive UI calls) to streaming tier.
2) Prefix / KV caching for repeated prompts (support templates) — expected token reduction 20–30%.
3) Start with a 3-month bridge commit at the balanced tier to prove token economics, then convert a portion of volume to dedicated capacity for predictable unit costs.

Attachments: I attached a short pricing sheet and a mutual action plan (MAP) with the proposed milestones.
[attachment: pricing-sheet.pdf (pdf)]
[attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (xlsx)]

Next steps (actionable):
- Alex: confirm whether $/1M token targets above (pick conservative band) — you mentioned a target near $600/1M for sustained volume.
- Procurement: let me know any mandatory procurement timelines or redlines for the MAP.
- Marissa/Ben: can you prepare an alternate routing example that shows cost delta at 200M / 400M / 1B tokens?

Thanks — happy to do a short follow-up with procurement to lock ranges.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
M: (555) 867-2400 | vivek@redwood.com

From: Alex Navarro <alex@insightai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@insightai.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: budgeting, SLO tiers & routing options

Vivek — great recap, and thanks to the team for the clear options. A few clarifications and answers from our side: 

1) Volume: for FY28 planning we want to target 500–750M tokens/month as our baseline (conservative). We may spike to ~1B in promotional months.
2) Latency: customer-facing chat (support portal) must target 95p <= 500ms (we can set 400ms as aspirational). Internal agent-to-agent workflows can tolerate 1s+ latency.
3) $/1M target: our budget owner asked if we can get to ~$450/1M sustained at ~500M+ committed. If not, we need to understand the delta (what gives us that rate: committed GPUs, quantized model variant, batching).
4) Compliance: SOC2 evidence is required. We expect standard artifacts + 12 months of audit logs.

Procurement note: We need a clear 30/60/90 day MAP with deliverables and a table of conservative vs aggressive pricing bands to present to finance. Also include any one-time onboarding fees.

I'll review the attachments and circle back by EOD Monday with our preferred target band and an internal approval timeline.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Navarro | Head of Platform Engineering | InsightAI
alex@insightai.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alex Navarro <alex@insightai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: budgeting, SLO tiers & routing options

Alex — perfect, that's helpful. Quick responses inline:

- Volume band: 500–750M sustained is exactly the scale where our balanced tier + a partial dedicated pool yields the best $/1M. I'll ask Marissa for a modeled example at 500M and 750M.
- $450/1M target: achievable with a combination of (a) a 12–36 month commit, (b) partially dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, and (c) using a 4-bit quantized model variant for non-critical prompts. The trade-offs: quality delta on a small subset of prompts (we can gate these).
- One-time fees: standard onboarding (including SOC2 handoff) — $12k engineering setup + optional private deployment setup (if you want VPC) — separate line item. I'll surface those in the MAP.

Suggested MAP milestones (high level):
1) Week 0–2: Sign mutual action plan, sign NDA/initial SOW (if needed).
2) Week 2–4: SOC2 artifact exchange and baseline integration (test keys, initial traces).
3) Week 4–8: Pilot (50–100M tokens) on balanced tier to validate latency/quality.
4) Week 8–12: Ramp to agreed committed band, enable dedicated pool/start commit discounts.

I attached a version of the MAP with placeholders for pricing bands — Marissa, Ben: please update the cost examples and a 3-band table (conservative / target / aggressive) for Alex's procurement deck.

If Alex can send the playbook for which calls require strict 400–500ms SLO vs. which can be relaxed, we can map the routing weights automatically.

I'll tentatively schedule a 30-min procurement review for Tue morning unless you prefer a different time.

— Vivek
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Alex Navarro <alex@insightai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: budgeting, SLO tiers & routing options

Adding a quick note on the SOC2 and retention ask:
- We'll provide the standard SOC2 evidence set and a signed statement of controls. Attached is a template response for the SOC2 questionnaire — that should speed review.
[attachment: soc2-questions.pdf (pdf)]

On pricing modeling: Marissa, I'll upload three scenario sheets to the shared Drive (conservative/target/aggressive) with explicit routing assumptions (percent streaming vs balanced vs batch) and show effective $/1M after cache/prefix savings. Vivek: want me to include a ride-rate schedule for converting to Dedicated capacity (monthly commit tiers)?

Alex: if you can share the list of endpoints that drive strict latency (e.g., live chat, in-app assistant) vs. background jobs, I'll label them in the MAP so the routing is deterministic.

Thanks — Ben
